hook: The FastAPI service from PY-13 needs a home: **Docker images, Azure pipelines, and secrets that never touch a config file.** The final mile of Stage 8.

scenes.title: Slim, multi-stage, reproducible: **the container contract**
scenes.sub: Small images, pinned bases, non-root, health-checked
scenes.narration: The Dockerfile that ships to production, discipline by discipline. MULTI-STAGE: a build stage with compilers and dev dependencies produces wheels; the final stage copies ONLY the runtime artifacts — images shrink from gigabytes to hundreds of megabytes, and attack surface shrinks with every dropped package. SLIM BASES: python:3.12-slim or distroless for the truly brave — 'latest' tags are forbidden; PIN the base image by digest — the same pinning philosophy as GA-26's models. NON-ROOT: create a user, drop privileges — a container running as root that escapes is a host compromise; as UID 10001, it's an annoyance. REPRODUCIBLE INSTALLS: requirements locked — uv.lock or pip-tools output — installed with no cache. And RUNTIME HYGIENE: a HEALTHCHECK endpoint — FastAPI's /healthz — so orchestrators know the truth; .dockerignore excluding .git, tests, and anything secrets-shaped — the image IS an artifact that gets stored, scanned, and possibly leaked — treat its contents as published.

scenes.title: Multi-stage Dockerfile for the FastAPI service
scenes.body:
# ---- build stage: compilers & dev deps live HERE only ----------
FROM python:3.12-slim AS build
WORKDIR /app
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir uv
COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock ./
RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev          # locked & reproducible

# ---- runtime stage: the smallest possible surface ----------------
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app
RUN groupadd -r app && useradd -r -g app app
COPY --from=build /app/.venv ./.venv
COPY ./app ./app
USER app                                # never root
EXPOSE 8000
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s \
  CMD python -c "import urllib.request;urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8000/healthz')"
CMD ["./.venv/bin/uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]
annot: uv.lock --frozen: the same dependency tree in every build, every environment — the model-pinning discipline for packages
The venv COPYs over, compilers don't: the runtime image has no gcc, no build headers — far fewer CVEs
HEALTHCHECK: orchestrators route on truth; without it, a hung service keeps receiving traffic
scenes.narration: Why each line earns its place: the lockfile makes builds reproducible — 'works on my machine' dies when the dependency graph is frozen; the multi-stage split means the image that RUNS contains no toolchain — scanners find less, attackers find less; the non-root user converts container escapes from catastrophe to inconvenience; and the healthcheck closes the loop with the platform — Azure Container Apps, Kubernetes, whatever — so traffic follows liveness, not hope. Two image-level habits complete it: SCAN in CI — Trivy or Grype against the image, failures block promotion, the same gate pattern as everything else; and LABEL — source repo, commit SHA, build time as OCI labels — when an incident involves an image, 'which code is running' must be a label read, not an archaeology dig. Small, pinned, non-root, health-checked, scanned, labeled — six adjectives that distinguish a container from a tarball.

scenes.title: Azure DevOps pipelines: **the same gates, now automated**
scenes.sub: Build → test → scan → deploy, with quality as a gate
scenes.narration: The pipeline embodies the whole curriculum's discipline in YAML. STAGES: BUILD — install with frozen lockfile, run ruff + black from PY-22's pre-commit set, compile-check, build the Docker image, tag with the commit SHA. TEST — pytest with PY-22's suites: unit tests with Fakes, and — the LKG signature — the eval gates: golden-set runs against the service, faithfulness thresholds, the agent regression suite from AG-18; failures here stop the line, exactly GA-26's promotion logic. SCAN — image vulnerability scan, dependency audit, secret scanning on the repo — nothing deploys with known-critical CVEs or a leaked key. DEPLOY — push the image to a registry — Azure Container Registry — then deploy via the pipeline to the target environment, with approvals between environments — the human checkpoint as a pipeline gate: dev deploys automatically, production requires an approver. ARTIFACTS AND TRACES: every run links commit → image digest → deployment — full provenance, GA-21's requirement, for the application layer.

layers.s: Locked deps · lint/format · image build · SHA tags
pytest + Fakes · EVAL GATES: golden set, faithfulness, agent regressions
Image CVEs · dependency audit · secret scanning
ACR push · env promotion with approvals · provenance: commit → digest → deploy

scenes.narration: The eval-gates-in-CI step is the one that makes an AI application pipeline DIFFERENT from a classical one: the test stage doesn't only assert code correctness — it asserts BEHAVIOR against golden datasets, exactly GA-26's environment promotion, running on every commit. Notice the symmetry the whole curriculum keeps drawing: prompts versioned like code, models pinned like dependencies, quality gated like tests, deployments promoted like releases — because AI systems are software systems whose behavior happens to be probabilistic; the engineering response is MORE discipline, not less. Pipeline hygiene: keep stages FAST — the build-and-unit stage under ten minutes, because slow gates get bypassed — push heavy eval suites to a scheduled nightly with PR-blocking smoke subsets, GA-21's fast-gate pattern one last time. And everything as CODE — azure-pipelines.yaml in the repo, reviewed, versioned, diffed.

scenes.title: Where it runs: App Service, Container Apps, Functions
scenes.sub: Matching the workload to the Azure compute shape
scenes.narration: Three Azure homes for the service, chosen by shape. APP SERVICE — the managed web platform: simplest path for a stateless FastAPI service — managed TLS, scaling, deployment slots for blue-green — right when you want PaaS convenience and your workload is a conventional web API. AZURE CONTAINER APPS — the container-native middle: run the exact Docker image with scale-to-zero, event-driven scaling from queues — AG-19's queue-consuming agents fit here perfectly: jobs arrive, containers spin up, scale away when quiet — you pay for use, and the durable-agent pattern gets a native home. AZURE FUNCTIONS — the function shape: event-triggered pieces — a webhook that kicks an agent run, a timer that launches the nightly eval suite — cheap, serverless, composable as glue around the bigger services. The selection logic: stateless API with steady traffic → App Service; queue-driven, spiky, container-shaped workloads → Container Apps; event glue and small triggers → Functions. Real systems mix: the API on App Service, the agent workers on Container Apps, the triggers on Functions — each piece on the cheapest shape that fits.

cards.s: Managed PaaS · TLS + slots · steady stateless APIs · least container ceremony
Your exact image · scale-to-zero · queue/event-driven agents · pay per use
Event glue · webhooks/timers · smallest triggers around the bigger pieces

scenes.narration: Two cross-cutting Azure practices whatever the target. Deployment slots: stage a release alongside production, swap when ready, swap BACK in ninety seconds if quality gates trip post-deploy — GA-26's feature-flag rollout, implemented by the platform; pair slot swaps with the shadow-eval discipline — run the golden set against the slot BEFORE the swap, and the promotion becomes boring, which is the goal. And scaling honesty: autoscaling reacts to load, not to cost — GA-24's per-feature cost dashboards tell you whether the scaling you're doing is profitable; a feature whose revenue doesn't cover its autoscale bill is a pricing conversation, not an infrastructure one. The deployment options are the easy part — the curriculum's real weight sits in everything the pipeline gates before a single container starts: the tests, the evals, the scans, the pins.

scenes.title: Key Vault & managed identity: **secrets that were never anywhere**
scenes.sub: The end of connection strings in environment variables
scenes.narration: The final discipline, and the most absolute: secrets never appear in code, config files, pipeline variables, or environment dumps. AZURE KEY VAULT: the store — API keys, database passwords, provider tokens — with access POLICIES controlling which identities may read which secrets, rotation history built in, and audit of every access. MANAGED IDENTITY: the mechanism that makes it clean — the Azure resource — your App Service, your Container App — gets an identity that IS an Azure AD principal; the application asks the platform for a token, the platform vouches for the resource, Key Vault releases the secret; NO credential is ever stored in the app — nothing to leak from a config, nothing to rotate in a hurry, nothing appearing in a support-bundle screenshot. The application code reads: 'get secret X from vault Y via my identity' — DefaultAzureCredential handles the dance. Rotation becomes a Key Vault operation, not a deployment: rotate the secret, the app picks up the new value on next fetch — the credential-lifecycle discipline from AG-07, implemented by the platform.

scenes.title: The application side: identity-based secret access
scenes.body:
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential
from azure.keyvault.secrets import SecretClient

# The app has NO secret in its config — only WHERE to ask.
credential = DefaultAzureCredential()          # the platform's identity
client = SecretClient(vault_url=VAULT_URL, credential=credential)

async def get_db_password() -> str:
    return client.get_secret("db-password").value

# Locally: DefaultAzureCredential falls back to your az CLI login.
# In Azure: the resource's managed identity vouches automatically.
# The pipeline: variable groups bound to Key Vault — same rule.
# Nowhere: a secret in a file, an env var dump, or a pipeline log.
annot: DefaultAzureCredential chains local dev (az login) → managed identity (Azure) — one code path, zero config forks
Variable groups bound to Key Vault bring the SAME discipline to pipeline variables — the leak surface shrinks everywhere at once
get_secret at runtime + short TTL caching: fresh secrets without a restart, rotation without a deployment
scenes.narration: What changes culturally when this is real: the 'where are the credentials' question disappears from onboarding, incident response, and audits — because the answer is a Key Vault access policy, reviewable and revocable in one place; the rotation drill — AG-07's playbook — becomes a five-minute platform operation instead of a cross-team scramble; and the whole class of 'secret committed to git' incidents — still among the most common breaches anywhere — becomes structurally impossible for the secrets that matter most. This closes Stage 8 the way the stage opened: with boundaries. The LLM traffic got a gateway; the agent actions got gates; the egress got allow-lists; and now the application's own credentials live in a vault, fetched by identity, never written down. Theory complete — Stages 9 and 10 turn it all into projects.

recap: Docker done right: multi-stage, slim pinned bases, locked deps, non-root, health-checked, scanned, labeled
Pipelines gate quality, not just code: eval suites block promotion; App Service / Container Apps / Functions matched to workload shape
Key Vault + managed identity: secrets fetched by platform vouching — never in code, config, or pipeline variables; rotation without deployment

quiz.q: What does multi-stage building buy beyond a smaller image?
opts: The runtime image carries no toolchain — fewer CVEs, smaller attack surface, faster scans — not just fewer megabytes
quiz.why: Every build-time package in the final image is a vulnerability-report line and an attacker opportunity — the split removes them by construction.

quiz.q: How do eval gates change a CI pipeline for AI applications?
opts: Behavior becomes a promotion gate — golden sets and agent regressions block deployment exactly like failing unit tests, on every commit
quiz.why: Code correctness alone can't gate a probabilistic system; the pipeline asserts BEHAVIOR the same disciplined way — smoke on PRs, full suites on schedule.

quiz.q: What makes managed identity fundamentally different from environment-variable secrets?
opts: No credential is ever stored in the app at all — the platform vouches for the resource, so there's nothing to leak, commit, or rotate in code
quiz.why: The secret's lifecycle — storage, access, rotation, audit — moves entirely to the platform; the application holds nothing worth stealing.

code.title: The pipeline definition — the whole reel in YAML
code.body:
# azure-pipelines.yml — build, gate, scan, deploy
trigger: [main]

stages:
  - stage: Build
    jobs:
      - script: |
          pip install uv && uv sync --frozen
          uv run ruff check --fix . && uv run black --check .
          uv run pytest tests/unit -q          # PY-22 suites + Fakes
        displayName: lint + unit tests
      - script: docker build -t $(acr)/app:$(Build.SourceVersion) .
        displayName: build image (SHA-tagged)

  - stage: EvalGate                 # the AI difference
    dependsOn: Build
    jobs:
      - script: uv run pytest tests/evals -q   # golden set, faithfulness,
        displayName: eval gates                # agent regressions (AG-18)

  - stage: Scan
    dependsOn: EvalGate
    jobs:
      - script: trivy image --severity HIGH,CRITICAL --exit-code 1 $(acr)/app:$(Build.SourceVersion)
        displayName: image CVE gate

  - stage: DeployProd
    dependsOn: Scan
    condition: succeeded()
    jobs:
      - deployment: swap
        environment: production              # approval gate here
        strategy: runOnce:
          deploy:
            steps:
              - script: az webapp deployment slot swap -g $(rg) -n $(app) --slot staging --target-slot production
annot: SHA tagging: the running image's identity is its git commit — provenance by construction (GA-21 discipline)
EvalGate between build and scan: behavior is gated BEFORE the image is even security-scanned for deployment
Slot swap with rollback: the ninety-second reverse gear — if post-deploy quality trips, swap back

notes:
# Packaging & Deployment

## Docker
- Multi-stage (no toolchain in runtime) · slim base PINNED by digest · locked deps (uv.lock --frozen) · non-root · HEALTHCHECK · scan + OCI labels.

## Azure DevOps pipelines
- Build → EvalGate (golden set, faithfulness, agent regressions) → Scan (image CVEs, deps, secrets) → Deploy with env approvals.
- Fast PR gates + nightly full suites; everything as YAML in the repo.

## Azure targets
- App Service: steady stateless APIs. Container Apps: queue/event-driven agents, scale-to-zero. Functions: event glue.
- Slots for blue-green + shadow eval before swap.

## Key Vault & managed identity
- Secrets fetched via DefaultAzureCredential — no credential in code/config/pipeline.
- Rotation = Key Vault operation; access policies reviewable; audit of every read.
